title: What happens to beached whales
titleChinese: 鲸鱼搁浅对我们有何启示？
paragraphs: In July 2024, a pod of 77 pilot whales washed up on a beach in Orkney, Scotland. It was the largest mass stranding of whales in Scotland for decades. Scientists don't know exactly why whales beach themselves. One theory is that climate change is driving whales' food closer to the shoreline, where they then get stuck as the tide goes out. If a single animal is found, it is usually because it is sick or has been injured.

In the Orkney stranding, 12 of the whales were still alive when they became beached. When this happens, marine organisations assess whether a whale can be safely refloated. Professionals and members of the community often come together, cover the animal in wet sheets and pour buckets of water over it, though not the blowhole, until the animal drifts back out to the ocean. Though it's not always a happy ending.

For those that don't survive, a post-mortem examination is often carried out. Dr Brownlow of the Scottish Marine Animal Stranding Scheme told the BBC that these can reveal a lot about the whale's life and the reasons why it was beached.

In 2024, a very rare species of whale turned up on a beach in New Zealand – a spade-toothed whale. While this is sad, the carcass was dissected in order to help researchers acquire new information about the species. "From a scientific and conservation point of view, this is huge", Gabe Davies, a Department of Conservation official, said.

Some beached whales who don't survive have their skeletons sent to museums, while many others are returned to the water. This ensures the marine environment benefits because whale carcasses give off many nutrients. "When they fall and die and sink to the bottom of the ocean, they form these little nutrient-rich islands that can support a huge diversity of life", says Dr Brownlow.
The more research that can be done, the better. For now, we can only do what we can to keep our oceans clean and safe.

vocabulary.example: A pod of dolphins swam alongside the boat.
vocabulary.translation: 一群海豚在船边游过。

vocabulary.example: Pilot whales are known for their strong social bonds.
vocabulary.translation: 领航鲸以其强大的社会纽带而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: **wash up** /ˌwɒʃ ˈʌp/ phr. v. （被浪）冲上岸（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Debris from the shipwreck washed up on the shore.
vocabulary.translation: 沉船的残骸被冲上了岸。

vocabulary.example: The stranding of whales is often caused by illness or navigational errors.
vocabulary.translation: 鲸鱼搁浅通常是由疾病或导航错误引起的。

vocabulary.example: The storm beached several boats along the coast.
vocabulary.translation: 风暴使几艘船在沿岸搁浅。

vocabulary.example: The shoreline has eroded significantly over the years.
vocabulary.translation: 多年来海岸线已明显被侵蚀。

vocabulary.example: The tide was coming in, covering the sand.
vocabulary.translation: 涨潮了，淹没了沙滩。

vocabulary.entry: **go out** /ˌɡəʊ ˈaʊt/ phr. v. （潮水）退去（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: We went for a walk on the beach when the tide went out.
vocabulary.translation: 退潮时我们去海滩散步了。

vocabulary.entry: **marine** /məˈriːn/ adj. 海洋的，海产的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Marine life is threatened by pollution.
vocabulary.translation: 海洋生物受到污染的威胁。

vocabulary.entry: **refloat** /ˌriːˈfləʊt/ v. 使（搁浅的船或动物）重新浮起
vocabulary.example: Efforts to refloat the stranded whale were unsuccessful.
vocabulary.translation: 让搁浅的鲸鱼重新浮起的努力没有成功。

vocabulary.entry: **blowhole** /ˈbləʊhəʊl/ n. （鲸、海豚等的）呼吸孔，喷水孔
vocabulary.example: The whale shot water from its blowhole.
vocabulary.translation: 鲸鱼从呼吸孔喷出水柱。

vocabulary.example: The boat drifted out to sea.
vocabulary.translation: 船漂向了外海。

vocabulary.entry: **post-mortem** /ˌpəʊst ˈmɔːtəm/ n. 验尸，尸检（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The post-mortem revealed the cause of death.
vocabulary.translation: 尸检揭示了死因。

vocabulary.example: The doctor carried out a thorough examination.
vocabulary.translation: 医生进行了全面检查。

vocabulary.example: The results revealed a surprising pattern.
vocabulary.translation: 结果揭示了一个令人惊讶的模式。

vocabulary.example: There are many species of birds in this forest.
vocabulary.translation: 这片森林里有许多种鸟类。

vocabulary.entry: **spade-toothed whale** /ˌspeɪd tuːθt ˈweɪl/ n. 铲齿鲸
vocabulary.example: The spade-toothed whale is one of the rarest whale species.
vocabulary.translation: 铲齿鲸是最稀有的鲸类物种之一。

vocabulary.example: Vultures were feeding on the lion's carcass.
vocabulary.translation: 秃鹫正在啄食狮子的尸体。

vocabulary.entry: **dissect** /daɪˈsekt/ v. 解剖（尸体）（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The biology students dissected a frog in class.
vocabulary.translation: 生物课的学生在课堂上解剖了一只青蛙。

vocabulary.example: She acquired a knowledge of French during her time in Paris.
vocabulary.translation: 她在巴黎期间学会了法语。

vocabulary.entry: **conservation** /ˌkɒnsəˈveɪʃn/ n. 保护（环境、动植物等）（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The group works on wildlife conservation.
vocabulary.translation: 该组织致力于野生动物保护。

vocabulary.example: The museum has a dinosaur skeleton on display.
vocabulary.translation: 博物馆里展出了一具恐龙骨架。

vocabulary.entry: **nutrient** /ˈnjuːtriənt/ n. 营养素，养分（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Plants absorb nutrients from the soil.
vocabulary.translation: 植物从土壤中吸收养分。

vocabulary.example: The soil is nutrient-rich and perfect for farming.
vocabulary.translation: 这片土壤营养丰富，非常适合耕种。

vocabulary.entry: **diversity** /daɪˈvɜːsəti/ n. 多样性，多样化（书面语）
vocabulary.example: There is a wide diversity of opinion on this issue.
vocabulary.translation: 关于这个问题存在广泛多样的意见。

sentences.english: In July 2024, a pod of 77 pilot whales washed up on a beach in Orkney, Scotland.
sentences.chinese: 2024年7月，一群由77头领航鲸组成的鲸群在苏格兰奥克尼群岛的一处海滩上搁浅。

sentences.english: It was the largest mass stranding of whales in Scotland for decades.
sentences.chinese: 这是苏格兰几十年来最大规模的鲸鱼集体搁浅事件。

sentences.english: Scientists don't know exactly why whales beach themselves.
sentences.chinese: 科学家们并不确切知道鲸鱼为什么会搁浅。

sentences.english: One theory is that climate change is driving whales' food closer to the shoreline, where they then get stuck as the tide goes out.
sentences.chinese: 一种理论认为，气候变化正将鲸鱼的食物驱赶到离海岸线更近的地方，然后当潮水退去时，它们就会被困在那里。

sentences.english: If a single animal is found, it is usually because it is sick or has been injured.
sentences.chinese: 如果发现的是单只动物，通常是因为它生病或受伤了。

sentences.english: In the Orkney stranding, 12 of the whales were still alive when they became beached.
sentences.chinese: 在奥克尼搁浅事件中，有12头鲸鱼搁浅时仍然活着。

sentences.english: When this happens, marine organisations assess whether a whale can be safely refloated.
sentences.chinese: 当这种情况发生时，海洋组织会评估鲸鱼能否被安全地送回海中。

sentences.english: Professionals and members of the community often come together, cover the animal in wet sheets and pour buckets of water over it, though not the blowhole, until the animal drifts back out to the ocean.
sentences.chinese: 专业人士和社区成员通常会聚集在一起，用湿布盖住鲸鱼，并用水桶往它身上浇水（但不浇呼吸孔），直到动物随潮水漂回大海。

sentences.english: Though it's not always a happy ending.
sentences.chinese: 不过，并不总是圆满结局。

sentences.english: For those that don't survive, a post-mortem examination is often carried out.
sentences.chinese: 对于那些未能存活的鲸鱼，通常会进行尸检。

sentences.english: Dr Brownlow of the Scottish Marine Animal Stranding Scheme told the BBC that these can reveal a lot about the whale's life and the reasons why it was beached.
sentences.chinese: 苏格兰海洋动物搁浅计划的布朗洛博士告诉BBC，这些检查可以揭示出关于鲸鱼生活以及其搁浅原因的很多信息。

sentences.english: In 2024, a very rare species of whale turned up on a beach in New Zealand – a spade-toothed whale.
sentences.chinese: 2024年，一种非常罕见的鲸鱼——铲齿鲸——在新西兰的一处海滩上被发现。

sentences.english: While this is sad, the carcass was dissected in order to help researchers acquire new information about the species.
sentences.chinese: 虽然这令人悲伤，但研究人员对这具尸体进行了解剖，以获取关于这一物种的新信息。

sentences.english: "From a scientific and conservation point of view, this is huge", Gabe Davies, a Department of Conservation official, said.
sentences.chinese: 新西兰环境保护部官员盖比·戴维斯说："从科学和保护的视角来看，这样做意义重大。"

sentences.english: Some beached whales who don't survive have their skeletons sent to museums, while many others are returned to the water.
sentences.chinese: 一些未能存活的搁浅鲸鱼的骨架会被送往博物馆，而其他许多鲸鱼则会被送回大海。

sentences.english: This ensures the marine environment benefits because whale carcasses give off many nutrients.
sentences.chinese: 这有助于海洋环境，因为鲸鱼尸体能释放出大量营养物质。

sentences.english: "When they fall and die and sink to the bottom of the ocean, they form these little nutrient-rich islands that can support a huge diversity of life", says Dr Brownlow.
sentences.chinese: 布朗洛博士说："当它们倒下死去并沉入海底时，就形成了这些富含营养的小岛屿，能够滋养多种多样的生命。"

sentences.english: The more research that can be done, the better.
sentences.chinese: 能够进行的研究越多越好。

sentences.english: For now, we can only do what we can to keep our oceans clean and safe.
sentences.chinese: 就目前而言，我们只能尽我们所能来保持海洋的清洁和安全。
